recommended.name: Application-owned Better Auth before hook with server-owned current authority and cookie-cache disabled
scope: Small application-owned helper if needed to keep lifecycle policy testable without circular auth import
Targeted tests and separately captured current-source evidence
requirements: Disable use of signed cookie cache for authority, including already-issued valid cache.
For protected own-account and optional get-session operations obtain fresh persisted session without inheriting prepopulated stale context or caller cache query; prevent recursive outer-hook calls.
Check current account by immutable current session subject for isActive and indefinite/future lock. Do not substitute full application RBAC.
Public initiation/recovery/callback/status and sign-out cleanup exceptions explicit. Custom update-user service remains authoritative.
Avoid refreshing session lifetime during admission; allow only separately reviewed own expired-session cleanup.
tradeoffs: Every protected auth request must reach persisted authority; extra local database query cost is accepted for immediate current-state correctness.
A global disable switch alone is insufficient for lifecycle state. Hook and config must be reviewed together.
No transaction-level revocation linearizability is claimed by a preflight query.

alternatives.name: Catch-all HTTP preflight while retaining cache
alternatives.assessment: Can close HTTP symptoms but leaves direct auth.api entry points requiring a separate equivalent policy, duplicates path normalization, and risks trusting provider-internal stale context after preflight. Prefer A for bounded shared enforcement.

alternatives.name: Disable cookie cache only
alternatives.assessment: Insufficient: fresh current session still returns inactive/locked current user unless account lifecycle is checked.

alternatives.name: Replace core auth admission with requireRbacContext
alternatives.assessment: Reject: it silently adds active tenant, email verification, role/permission and module-adjacent constraints to own-account/public recovery semantics.

rollback.source: Restore only reviewed R06-owned hunks/helper/tests if repair is reverted; preserve unrelated working-tree modifications.
rollback.data: No schema change or production migration required. Retain isolated native receipts and fixture database; clean only owned sessions/runtime processes.
rollback.security: Reverting reopens confirmed V02 current-authority defects; do not describe rollback as production acceptance.
